title: Analyzing mouse neural stem cell and progenitor cell proliferation using EdU incorporation and multicolor flow cytometry
protocol: Decapitate mouse pup and remove the brain.
Transfer the brain to a 60 mm plastic dish containing ice-cold PGM.
Cut coronal sections by making incisions at ∼2 mm and ∼5 mm from the anterior end of the brain, discarding the olfactory bulb.
Move the resulting ∼3 mm section to a clean 60 mm plastic dish and keep it submerged in ice-cold PGM.
Use curved #7 Dumont forceps to gently move the slices to a dish containing cold PGM.
Place the dish under a dissecting scope with the posterior side facing up.
Remove the hippocampus to expose the ventricle.
Make the first incision between the corpus callosum and top of the lateral ventricle.
Make the second incision parallel to the wall of the lateral ventricle.
Make the third incision parallel to the medial wall of the ventricle.
Remove the target region containing the SVZ and place it in a clean dish with ice-cold PGM.
Mince the SVZ enriched tissue into cubes less than 1 mm using forceps.
Transfer the minced tissue to a 15 mL conical polypropylene centrifuge tube with a wide-bore pipet tip, rinsing the dish with PGM to collect all tissue.
Centrifuge at 200×g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant from the tube.
Add 2 mL of digestion buffer and resuspend the pellet carefully.
Incubate the tube at 37°C under agitation for 30 minutes.
Add 2 mL of inactivation buffer to the tube after incubation.
Centrifuge at 200×g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant from the tube.
Shatter the pellet by firmly striking the tip of the tube against the tissue culture hood.
Add 3 mL of PGB and gently triturate the tissue by pipetting up and down with a P1000 wide bore tip 5 times.
Allow debris to settle down for 5 minutes.
Transfer 2 mL of supernatant to a 50 mL conical tube passing through a 100 μm cell strainer (previously rinsed with PGB).
Add 2 mL of fresh PGB to the original cell tube and triturate using a standard P1000 tip approximately 15 times.
Pass all of the solution through a 100 μm filter (cell strainer) into the same 50 mL tube.
Rinse the cell strainer with PGB bringing the volume in the 50 mL conical tube to 25 mL.
Centrifuge at 200×g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Remove supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of PGB.
Keep the cells on ice.
Determine the number of viable cells using an automated cell counter or hemocytometer.
Transfer 1 × 10^6 viable cells, in 50 μL of PGB, to a 1 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Prepare 3 additional 1 mL tubes with 1 × 10^5 cells in 50 μL of PGB.
Add 1 μL of Fc Receptor block (1/50) to each tube.
Incubate on ice for 10 min.
For the sample tube, add the necessary volumes of each primary antibody to reach the dilutions specified.
Increase the final volume to 150 μL of PGB.
For isotypes or unstained samples, add the same amount of isotype fluorophore controls as used for primary antibodies.
Alternatively, omit adding isotypes and increase the volume to 150 μL with PGB.
Add 100 μL of PGB to the Live/Dead tube.
Remove half of the total volume and incubate at 65°C for 5 min.
Cool on ice.
Return heat-killed cells to original tube, reconstituting the 150 μL in the Live/Dead tube.
Keep on ice until step 25.
Incubate all tubes on ice for 20 min (protected from light).
Centrifuge at 300×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant.
Resuspend in 200 μl PGB for the first wash.
Repeat steps 19–21 for a second wash, resuspending cells in 150 μl PGB.
Add secondary antibody to sample tube according to Table 2.
Incubate for 25 min on ice (protected from light).
Wash 2× with PGB as in steps 19–21.
Fix cells by adding 1% fresh PFA in PBS without Ca²⁺ or Mg²⁺ and incubate for 20 min on ice.
Centrifuge cells at 300×g for 8 min at 4°C and remove supernatant.
Resuspend pellet with PBS without Ca²⁺ or Mg²⁺.
Centrifuge cells at 300×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend cells in 100 μl of 1× Click-It saponin-based permeabilization and wash reagent.
Incubate for 15 min.
Prepare Click-iT reaction cocktail according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Add 150 μL of Click-iT reaction cocktail to each well.
Incubate for 30 min at room temperature, protected from light.
Centrifuge cell at 300×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard supernatant and wash cells with 200 μL of PGB.
Centrifuge cells at 300×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard supernatant and resuspend pellet in 1 mL of PGB.
Keep at 4°C until ready to load into flow cytometer.
Run samples through the flow cytometer to evaluate cell phenotype and EdU incorporation.
Separate SVZs from 12 to 15 mice at P5 by dissection.
Pool the dissected SVZ samples together.
Dissociate pooled SVZ samples into single cells.
Stain dissociated cells for flow cytometry analysis.
Identify single, viable cells using side-scatter (SSC-A) versus forward scatter (FSC-A) gating.
Separate single cells from doublets based on SSC-H vs SSC-A.
Identify viable cells based on negative DAPI or Live/Dead staining.
Classify subpopulations of SVZ neural progenitors using a double gating strategy for CD140a and NG2 expression.
Remove debris based on SSC vs. FSC gating criteria.
Remove doublets by gating on FSC-H vs. FSC-A or SSC-H vs. SSC-A.
Select live cells by gating on the DAPI negative population using a Live/Dead (DAPI only) sample to set this gate.
Use the isotype control tube to set the thresholds for positively stained cells for NG2, CD140a, CD15, and CD133.
Create gate inclusion criteria for all populations listed based on antigenic profiles provided.
Set the gate for EdU using cells from mice that had not received EdU.
Determine the percentage of EdU+ cells for each subpopulation of neural progenitors.
Run all experimental samples, recording at least 100,000 events for each tube.
Record data for all required channels.
Use isotype antibodies to define thresholds for positive cells, ensuring that 2% of viable cells are included in the positive gates.
